question: When did the Green Revolution begin in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1966**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India began in **1966**, primarily focusing on increasing agricultural productivity to address food shortages and achieve self-sufficiency in food grain production.
 
• It introduced **high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds** for wheat and rice, along with improved irrigation methods, fertilizers, and pesticides to enhance crop yields.
 
• The initiative was launched during the Third Five-Year Plan (1961–1966), with the formal adoption of HYV seeds starting in **1966**.
 
• Dr. Norman Borlaug, known as the "Father of the Green Revolution," was instrumental globally, while Dr. M.S. Swaminathan led its implementation in India.
 
• The Green Revolution initially benefited regions like Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh due to their favorable irrigation infrastructure and climatic conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Main Theme:**

 
 
• The Green Revolution refers to the period of agricultural transformation aimed at increasing food grain production through the introduction of HYV seeds, chemical fertilizers, irrigation facilities, and modern farming techniques.
 
• While it brought significant benefits, such as self-sufficiency in food production and poverty reduction, it also led to challenges like environmental degradation, regional disparities, and increased reliance on chemical inputs.
